rationale: iter-1 baseline-reproduce (resnet 6 blocks c=32) FAILED on node lme171 - NVML driver/library version mismatch (cluster infra). Slurm exit code 18 means node failure; this is not a solver bug.
iter-2 baseline-reproduce on lme50 (GTX 1080 Ti, slow) TIMED OUT at 8:08 / 10:00 wall. The residual stack needs ~7 min on slow GPUs; 5-min budget is unrealistic without GPU pinning.

iter-3: swapped Wagner-2022 MSE for Charbonnier loss (eps=1e-3) on the Agent-B iter-2 residual-stack baseline (6 blk c=32, GroupNorm, ReLU; same arch, 0.225M params). Headroom 0.5831 (Agent B MSE) -> 0.5606 (-3.9%). Same pattern as main-agent iter-6: L1-flavored losses (Charbonnier behaves like L1 for residuals >> eps=1e-3) trade pixel-RMSE for perceptual sharpness. Pentathlon scores headroom -> discard.
Huber loss with delta=1e-3 on residual-stack baseline. Hypothesis: most pixel errors stay in quadratic regime (preserving RMSE) and only outliers get L1.
Huber loss with delta=1e-4 (10x smaller than iter-4) on residual-stack baseline. Smaller delta narrows L1 zone, expanding quadratic regime to match MSE behavior on most pixel errors.

iter-6: train_n 400 -> 600 (+50% data) at MSE loss (reverted after Huber experiments). Headroom 0.5807 (iter-25 baseline) -> 0.5689 (-1.18pp), val_rmse +3.4%. Training time 432s -> 638s (+48%, scales linearly). With model capacity fixed at 0.225M and 8-epoch budget, adding 50% more phantoms means each one is seen ~33% fewer times -> undertraining. Discard, revert.

iter-7: image-space D4 phantom augmentation (rot90 x hflip x vflip = 16 transforms). Per-epoch single global random transform applied to the 400 phantoms, re-projected through R_full (identical fan-beam geometry), with fresh per-epoch noise seed. Headroom 0.5807 (iter-25 baseline) -> 0.5730 (-0.78pp). val_rmse 0.005537 -> 0.005640 (+1.9%). Training loss monotonically decreased (0.00041 -> 0.00037 - the lowest of any iter) so the model fits the augmented distribution fine; the regression is val-side. Two likely culprits: (a) global per-epoch aug gives the model only 8 random orientations in 8 epochs, with insufficient repetition for any single orientation; (b) D4 includes 90 and 270 rotations that produce vertically-oriented bodies (the ellipses_phantom body outline is 0.85 x 0.65 horizontal), which the validation set never contains -> partial OOD training. Discard, revert.

iter-8: restrict augmentation to hflip+vflip only (4 transforms incl. identity), no rotation, after iter-7 D4 regressed -0.78pp. Hypothesis: 90/270 rotations made the body vertical (OOD vs validation), removing them recovers most of the headroom. Result: headroom 0.5807 baseline -> 0.5779 (-0.28pp). val_rmse +0.7%. Confirms the rotation hypothesis (regression shrank from -0.78pp to -0.28pp by dropping rot90) but per-epoch global flip-only aug still regresses. The remaining -0.28pp likely comes from the model under-training on the identity orientation: with 8 epochs each showing a single global transform, the validation orientation (identity) is seen on average only 2 epochs out of 8, and the loss is shared with 6 epochs of flipped data. Augmentation as a class appears exhausted at this per-epoch granularity / 8-epoch budget. Discard, revert.
Per-batch flip augmentation: hflip OR vflip applied per training batch instead of per-epoch (finer granularity).

MIXUP at phantom level: sample two phantoms per batch, mix with lambda~Beta(0.4,0.4), re-project mixed phantom, simulate noise. Stays in random-ellipse distribution (sum of ellipses is another valid phantom) unlike flips which were OOD.
SWA over last 2 epochs (Izmailov+ 2018). Snapshot at end of epoch 7 and 8, average parameters before validation. GroupNorm so no BN-stat refresh needed.
Cosine LR schedule 1e-4 -> 1e-6 over 8 epochs (Loshchilov 2017). Complement to SWA: flat optimum naturally without snapshot averaging.
Bump lr 1e-4 -> 2e-4. Iter-11/12 suggested model LR-limited. Test 2x learning rate at constant schedule.
ReLU -> GELU activation in residual blocks. GELU is smooth + nonzero gradient everywhere, used in NAFNet/Restormer/recent CT-denoising SOTA. Same param count.
epochs 8 -> 10 (more training steps). Hypothesis: model is undertrained because loss still actively decreasing at epoch 8.
weight_decay 1e-4 -> 1e-3 (10x). iter-15 showed pipeline overfits dual-domain noise target. Stronger AdamW wd specifically penalizes weights that encode noise.
wd 1e-3 -> 3e-3 to bracket the regularization sweet spot.
Add light dropout=0.05 to residual blocks on top of wd=1e-3. Stack two regularization mechanisms.
Widen channels 32 -> 48 (~2.25x params, 0.225M -> 0.503M) on top of iter-16 wd=1e-3 KEEP.
EMA shadow weights decay=0.999, swap at validation. Standard in diffusion/NAFNet/Restormer.
EMA decay 0.99 (lower than iter-20 0.999) for shorter effective lookback ~100 steps.
gradient clipping max_norm=1.0 on top of iter-16 wd=1e-3 KEEP. Different regularization mechanism: caps per-step update magnitude.
Bisect wd between 1e-3 (KEEP iter-16) and 3e-3 (DISCARD iter-17): test wd=2e-3.
Per-batch i0 noise jitter [3e4, 8e4]. Train across noise range, val at fixed 5e4.

iter-25: res_kernel 3 -> 5 in residual blocks. TIMEOUT at 15min wall (15:00 / 15:00). Got to epoch 5/8 before SIGTERM. Param count 0.225M -> 0.620M (2.78x), train time grew 470s -> >900s. Cluster-wide finding: kernel=5 with 6 residual blocks at c=32 is infeasible at 10-15 min wall (main iter-40 had same timeout at 10min).

iter-26: revert kernel 5 -> 3 + add 1 BF tail on residual stack (cross-port from main/A NAFNet+BF +0.04..+0.28pp curve). Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5710 (-1.23pp). DISCARD. BF tail does NOT transfer from NAFNet substrate to residual-stack substrate. Cross-substrate failure: BF compounding is NAFNet-specific (likely due to NAFNet's LN output statistics being more BF-amenable than resnet's residual-noise prediction).

iter-27: revert iter-26 BF + add EDSR per-block alpha (res_scale_init=0.1) cross-port from Agent B iter-14 KEEP +0.22pp. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5810 (-0.23pp). Just-DISCARD. Per-block alpha does NOT cross-port. Likely reason: Agent B's substrate has wd=1e-4 (mild) but C has wd=1e-3 (strong) — wd=1e-3 penalizes alpha values into ~0, killing the EDSR scaling. Cross-port requires wd_split treatment (exclude alpha from wd).

iter-28: res_scale_init=0.1 + wd_split (alpha/norm/bias wd=0) on loss-slug iter-16 substrate. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5827 (-0.06pp). Just-DISCARD but near-flat. wd_split rescued the alpha cross-port from -0.23pp (iter-27) to -0.06pp — alpha is no longer killed by wd=1e-3, but the residual mechanism isnt adding lift here. Likely the iter-16 substrate is already near-optimal in its capacity-vs-regularization trade-off.

iter-29: revert alpha=0 + keep wd_split (norm/bias excluded from wd=1e-3). Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5637 (-1.97pp). STRONG DISCARD. wd_split alone (without alpha mechanism) HURTS by 2pp on this slug. Counter-intuitive cross-substrate finding: on Agent B (wd=1e-4 low) wd_split is KEEP +0.22pp, on Agent C (wd=1e-3 high) wd_split is -1.97pp. The high-wd regime apparently NEEDS norm scales / biases regularized to control. The alpha cross-port pseudo-rescued by adding free-growing params (iter-28 -0.06pp) but this is now revealed as compensating for wd_split bug, not a true alpha lift.

iter-30: AdamW beta2 0.999 -> 0.99 (faster forget of past gradient stats) on iter-16 substrate. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5746 (-0.87pp). DISCARD. Beta2 axis closed: default 0.999 is the optimum for AdamW on this short-training (8 ep) substrate. Faster-forget beta2 doesn't help because the model isn't navigating noisy late-training dynamics — it's still actively improving at every epoch.

iter-31: batch_size 1 -> 2 on iter-16 substrate. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5558 (-2.75pp). STRONG DISCARD. With fixed 8-epoch budget, batch=2 halves effective steps (400 -> 200) and under-trains the model. The basin needs ~3200 steps total; halving them gives an unrecovered ~0.0002 final training loss vs ~0.00037 at batch=1.

iter-32: input_dropout 0.0 -> 0.05 on iter-16 substrate. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5721 (-1.12pp). DISCARD. Same finding as Agent B iter-48 (-0.75pp): input-noise injection hurts the dual-domain pipeline. Cross-substrate confirmed.

iter-33: res_residual True -> False on iter-16 substrate (predict output directly, not noise residual). Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5590 (-2.43pp). STRONG DISCARD. Zero-init tail means network outputs 0 at init; predicting full image from 0 takes far more epochs than predicting noise correction at 8-epoch budget. The zero-init + residual is critical for fast convergence.

iter-34: lr 1e-4 -> 5e-5 (half; probes lower side of basin) on iter-16 substrate. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5737 (-0.96pp). DISCARD. LR axis fully bisected: 5e-5=-0.96pp / 1e-4=KEEP / 2e-4=-0.30pp (iter-13). Optimum tight at 1e-4.
iter-35: AdamW eps 1e-8 -> 1e-6 on iter-16 substrate. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5665 (-1.68pp). DISCARD. Larger eps damps adaptive learning rates too aggressively. Default 1e-8 is the optimum.

iter-36: optimizer adamw (wd=1e-3) -> adam (wd=0) on iter-16 substrate. Headroom 0.5833 -> 0.5842 (+0.09pp). Marginal KEEP. Adam-with-no-wd slightly beats AdamW with the prior KEEP wd=1e-3. This contradicts iter-16's wd=1e-3 KEEP (now revealed as near-noise +0.26pp vs wd=1e-4 baseline). The true optimum is wd=0 (Adam) by ~0.09pp.

iter-37: Adam optimizer + weight_decay 0 -> 1e-4 (L2-via-grad style) on iter-36 substrate. Headroom 0.5842 -> 0.5158 (-6.84pp). STRONG DISCARD. Adam's wd is L2-via-grad (wd*w added inside grad) rather than decoupled (AdamW). With this regime any positive wd grows with parameter magnitude per step, destabilising training. Adam wants wd=0 strictly.

iter-38: adamw_eps 1e-8 -> 1e-10 (cross-port from B iter-53 KEEP +0.06pp) on Adam+wd=0 substrate. Headroom 0.5842 -> 0.5662 (-1.80pp). DISCARD. Tighter eps amplifies adaptive lr noise on Adam (no wd) more than on AdamW (with wd). Cross-substrate finding: eps sweet spot depends on wd state.

iter-39: revert optimizer adam -> adamw + wd 1e-3 -> 5e-4 (bisect between Adam wd=0 KEEP 0.5842 and AdamW wd=1e-3 0.5833). Headroom 0.5842 -> 0.5666 (-1.76pp). DISCARD. The bisection doesnt form a smooth curve: Adam (wd=0) is the new best, AdamW wd=5e-4 is much worse. Likely the AdamW switch reintroduces the bigger eps default effect. Adam (wd=0) remains best.

iter-40: lr 1e-4 -> 8e-5 (fine bisection lower) on Adam substrate iter-36. Headroom 0.5842 -> 0.5860 (+0.18pp). KEEP. NEW SLUG BEST. Lower wd means less effective regularization, so smaller lr to compensate.
